new_statements.quote: Syllables may begin or end with either vowels or consonants; e.g., na? what?; nal, road; gami, you all; awa, rope ... There is no apparent rule or uniformity of accent. Some words are distinguished only by difference of accent, e.g., bihi, to bind; bihi, a cave. The pronunciation of each word is an individual matter.
new_statements.citation: Paton, W.F. 1971. Ambrym (Lonwolwol) Grammar. Pacific Linguistics B-19. Canberra: The Australian National University.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Confirmed verbatim. (Paton 1971, PL B-19), p.12 'SYLLABLES AND ACCENT' par. 2, text layer lines 992-1003 and page image : 'Syllables may begin or end with either vowels or consonants; e.g., na? what?; nal, road; gami, you all; awa, rope; nornor, think. There is no apparent rule or uniformity of accent. Some words are distinguished only by difference of accent, e.g., bihi, to bind; bihi, a cave [accent marks on different syllables in the image]. The pronunciation of each word is an individual matter.' The reader's ellipsis only drops 'nornor, think'. As a reading of Paton this is correctly 'lexical (unpredictable)', and that is how it already stands in the catalog under lonw1238. IDEN…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No positional rule: accent placement is a property of the individual word (lexical), and accent alone can distinguish words (bíhi 'to bind' vs bihí 'a cave', accent marks as in Paton 1973:15).
new_statements.exceptions: None; only the accent minimal pair bihi/bihi is given.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms; missionary description (fieldwork 1933-48, thesis 1956) of the West Ambrym language of Dip Point / Craig Cove that Paton called 'Lonwolwol'. CAVEAT: this statement is already catalogued under lonw1238; it applies to dalk1234 only on the identification Dalkalaen (von Prince) = West Ambrym/'Lonwolwol' (Paton), which rests on both sources locating the language in the Craig Cove region (Lynch & Crowley 2001:94; TLA deposit description) rather than on an explicit equation read in von Prince 2015:2-4. No description of Dalkalaen phonology under that name exists in print.
new_statements.identity_note: dalk1234 'Dalkalaen' is Kilu von Prince's name (DoBeS 2009-12) for the West Ambrym language of 'the Craig Cove region, the westernmost region of Ambrym' (TLA deposit description). Paton's 'Lonwolwol' (lonw1238, ISO crc) is the language of 'Dip Point and Craig Cove' / 'the south-west of the island' (Paton 1971: iii, 128), which Lynch & Crowley 2001:94 call simply 'West Ambrym.. Craig Cove area on the western tip.. apparently has no name'. The two glottocodes therefore appear to denote one language (Glottolog doublet: dalk1234 was created from von Prince 2015:2-4 without an ISO code). The only stress statement (Paton 1971:12) is already catalogued under lonw1238; proposed for the catalogis set false to avoid counting one description twice. If the catalog keeps dalk1234 as a separate key, it should either be aliased to lonw1238 or left empty pending von Prince's unpublished Dalkalaen sketch; von Prince 2015:2-4 should be read to confirm the equation. Von Prince also notes the Dalkalaen region has the most internal dialect variation of West Ambrym; Paton distinguishes LON (Lonwolwol) and CC (Craig Cove) as dialects.

sources.note: 'There is no apparent rule or uniformity of accent. Some words are distinguished only by difference of accent, e.g., bihi, to bind; bihi, a cave. The pronunciation of each word is an individual matter.' Describes 'the language spoken in the south-west of the island' (editors' intro p.iii); Paton's 1937 primer is titled 'Bua ta Lonwolwol (Dip Point and Craig Cove)'.

sources.note: Identity evidence, not a stress source: lists Dalkalaen (1000 spk, no ISO) and Raljago = West Ambrym/Lonwolwol (crc, <10 spk) as separate languages, refuting the dalk1234 = lonw1238 doublet assumption used to transfer Paton 1971 to this key; the catalog's identity note for dalk1234/lonw1238 should cite it.

sources.note: No stress statement. Identity evidence: the West Ambrym language 'is spoken in a number of villages in the Craig Cove area on the western tip of Ambrym.. apparently has no name. While Paton often refers to it as Lonwolwol.. Craig Cove, Dip Point and Fanting' are also used; lists Paton 1971a/1973, Ray 1926:333-347, Codrington 1885, von der Gabelentz 1873 as its descriptions.

Intro: 'Lonwolwol, spoken in the south-west of the island'; five Ambrym languages listed (North Ambrym, Lonwolwol, Dakaka (Sesivi), Port Vato, South-East Ambrym).
